added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(x\), suppress it from the notation, put \(r=\operatorname{rank}(G)\), and order the eigenvalues of both Gram matrices decreasingly.  For every unit vector \(v\), the definition of the operator norm gives
\[
 |v^{\mathsf T}(\widehat G-G)v|\leq\delta. \tag{1}
\]
Applying (1) to the minimum over unit vectors in each subspace and then to the maximum over subspaces in the finite-dimensional variational characterization of an ordered eigenvalue gives
\[
 |\widehat\lambda_s-\lambda_s|\leq\delta,
 \qquad 1\leq s\leq p. \tag{2}
\]
This step follows directly because adding a function uniformly bounded in absolute value by \(\delta\) changes either a minimum or a maximum by at most \(\delta\).  By the projection-Gram gap, \(\lambda_s\geq\varepsilon\) for \(s\leq r\) and \(\lambda_s=0\) for \(s>r\).  Thus, on \(\delta<\varepsilon/4\),
\[
 \widehat\lambda_s>3\varepsilon/4>\tau_G\quad(s\leq r),
 \qquad
 \widehat\lambda_s<\varepsilon/4<\tau_G\quad(s>r). \tag{3}
\]
Equation (3) proves rank selection without using \(r\) in the algorithm.

Let
\[
 \widetilde G=\sum_{s:\,\widehat\lambda_s>\tau_G}
 \widehat\lambda_s\widehat v_s\widehat v_s^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Then \(\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}=\widetilde G^+\).  On the event in (3), all discarded fitted eigenvalues are at most \(\delta\), so
\[
 \|\widetilde G-\widehat G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\delta,
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2\delta. \tag{4}
\]
Moreover, \(\widetilde G\) and \(G\) have rank \(r\),
\[
 \|\widetilde G^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}leq2\varepsilon^{-1},
 \qquad
 \|G^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}leq\varepsilon^{-1}. \tag{5}
\]
For symmetric matrices \(A\) and \(H\) of equal rank, multiplication of the four Penrose identities yields the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 H^+-A^+={}&-H^+(H-A)A^+
 +H^{+2}(H-A)(I-AA^+)\\
 &+(I-H^+H)(H-A)A^{+2}. \tag{6}
\end{aligned}
\]
Use \(H=\widetilde G\), \(A=G\), (4), (5), and the fact that both complementary projections in (6) have operator norm at most one.  The three terms are bounded respectively by
\[
 4\varepsilon^{-2}\delta,qquad
 8\varepsilon^{-2}\delta,qquad
 2\varepsilon^{-2}\delta.
\]
Their sum is \(14\varepsilon^{-2}\delta\), proving the pointwise stability assertion.

It remains to remove the pointwise good-event restriction for the integrated bound.  The threshold definition always gives
\(\|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/\varepsilon\), while the gap gives \(\|G^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1/\varepsilon\).  Hence the inverse difference is at most \(3/\varepsilon\) where \(\delta\geq\varepsilon/4\).  Also,
\[
 P_X(\delta\geq\varepsilon/4)^{1/2}
 \leq4\varepsilon^{-1}\|\delta\|_{L^2(P_X)}. \tag{7}
\]
The \(L^2(P_X)\) norm on the good set is at most \(14\varepsilon^{-2}\|\delta\|_2\), and (7) bounds the bad-set contribution by \(12\varepsilon^{-2}\|\delta\|_2\).  The triangle inequality proves the constant \(26\).  Finally, \(r_{G,\infty}=o_P(1)\) implies \(P(r_{G,\infty}<\varepsilon/4)\to1\); equation (3) then proves the last assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For a foldwise coherent fit, put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\), coordinatewise.  Define the analysis event
\[
 \mathcal E_{\mathrm{supp},n}=
 \left\{\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x,a,j:\,M_A(x)_{aj}=0}
 \widehat M_A(x)_{aj}\leq\tau_{S,n},\quad
 \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x,z,j:\,M_Z(x)_{zj}=0}
 \widehat M_Z(x)_{zj}\leq\tau_{S,n}\right\},
\]
where the supremum of an empty set is zero.  If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), then \(P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{supp},n})\to1\).  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{supp},n}\),
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A+r_Z)\|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}+r_Ar_Z
 +\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\right].
\]
If the two measurement supports are supplied by the observed design and imposed on the fit, the last two terms are zero.  Thus unknown-support leakage is explicit and estimable rather than silently excluded.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For each training fold, fit one label-aligned product factorization represented by \(\widehat\eta\) on the declared outcome support \(\mathcal Y\), without imposing any unknown zero pattern on \(\widehat M_A\) or \(\widehat M_Z\).  Impose only fitted-law, hence computable, half-margin restrictions:
\[
 \min_j\widehat\pi_j\geq \varepsilon/2,\qquad
 \min_{a,z}\widehat d_{az}\geq \varepsilon/2,\qquad
 \sigma_{\min}(\widehat M_A)\wedge\sigma_{\min}(\widehat M_Z)\geq\varepsilon/2,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat R^{\mathsf T}\widehat D\widehat R)\geq\varepsilon/2.
\]
Set \(\widehat W=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat w)\), \(\widehat B=\widehat M_A\odot\widehat M_Z\), \(\widehat d=\widehat B\widehat w\), \(\widehat D=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat d)\), \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\),
\[
 \widehat N=I_{K^2}-\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B
 (\widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B)^+
 \widehat B^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad \widehat h=\widehat N\widehat c,
\]
and form \(\widehat G\), \(\widehat b_{(\cdot)}\), and \(\widehat b_U\) as implications of this same fitted product law.  With the fixed, known threshold \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), use the spectral-thresholded inverse \(\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\) and define
\[
 \widehat Qf_0=\widehat Nf_0-
 \widehat h^{\mathsf T}\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}
 \widehat b_{f_0}.
\]
Choose the support-screen threshold \(\tau_{S,n}\) using only the fold size and training data, and report the estimable leakage allowances \(\ell_{A,n}\) and \(\ell_{Z,n}\) from the fitted measurement probabilities.  Neither the true supports of \(M_A,M_Z\), the true Gram matrix \(G\), nor \(\operatorname{rank}(G)\) is queried by the fitting algorithm.  If measurement support sets are supplied as observed design information, the fit may optionally impose those known zeros and then the corresponding leakage allowance is zero; this is an optional specialization, not a requirement.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The current construction uses unknown measurement supports and the unknown true Gram rank. The replacement uses only fitted-law constraints, a fixed spectral cutoff, and estimable leakage diagnostics.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Let
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}
 =\frac{r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}}{\tau_{S,n}},
\]
and set
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_{\Sigma}={}&r_m+r_\pi+r_A+r_Z+r_f+r_w+r_W+r_B+r_d+r_D+r_R+r_N+r_h+r_G+r_b\\
 &+r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}+r_{G,\infty}
 +\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}+\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n},\\
 \Delta_n={}&r_m(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z)+r_Ar_Z
 +(r_A+r_Z)R_{\Sigma}+\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(r_{A,\infty}\), \(r_{Z,\infty}\), and \(r_{G,\infty}\) are the foldwise essential-supremum errors of \(\widehat M_A\), \(\widehat M_Z\), and \(\widehat G\), respectively.  The term \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) makes the support-screening event have probability tending to one, while \(\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\) records the first-order bias that can remain when an unrestricted fitted law puts mass in a true structural-zero cell.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Without design-known supports, fitted mass in true structural-zero cells survives the conditional-zero calculation at first order. The corrected remainder exposes that leakage and the rates needed for support screening and spectral selection.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Use \(\mathfrak F\) as follows.  On \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\), fit one tensor-product B-spline product likelihood for \((\pi,M_A,M_Z,f)\) with \(s_n\asymp n^{(d_X+1)/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\), allowing unrestricted measurement supports unless support sets are supplied as observed design information.  Choose from the \(K!\) common permutations the maximizer of the empirical training-sample minimum diagonal-minus-largest-off-diagonal self-report probability.  Enforce only the fitted half-margin inequalities in the coherent-fit definition, choose \(\tau_{S,n}\) without true-support information, set \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), and derive \(w,W,B,d,D,R,N,h,G,b_{(\cdot)},b_U\), \(\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\), \(Q\), and the leakage allowances by the displayed plug-in identities.  The output contains one fitted product law and does not take a true support, the true \(G\), or a true rank as an input.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The implementation handle must instantiate the non-oracle support diagnostic and spectral cutoff used by the corrected coherent fit.

proposed.name: Data-driven conditional Gram inverse
proposed.construction:
For a fitted conditional Gram matrix with spectral decomposition
\[
 \widehat G(x)=\sum_{s=1}^{2K^2}\widehat\lambda_s(x)
 \widehat v_s(x)\widehat v_s(x)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad \widehat\lambda_1(x)\geq\cdots\geq\widehat\lambda_{2K^2}(x)\geq0,
\]
set \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\) and define the Borel spectral functional
\[
 \widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}(x)
 =\sum_{s:\,\widehat\lambda_s(x)>\tau_G}
 \widehat\lambda_s(x)^{-1}
 \widehat v_s(x)\widehat v_s(x)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus the fitted rank is the observable count \(\widehat r_G(x)=\sum_s\mathbf 1\{\widehat\lambda_s(x)>\tau_G\}\); neither \(G(x)\) nor its rank is an input.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimator needs an explicit rank-free Gram solve.

proposed.name: Estimable measurement-support leakage allowances
proposed.construction:
Fix a positive, training-fold-measurable threshold \(\tau_{S,n}\downarrow0\) that is chosen without the true measurement supports.  In the absence of design-known supports, define
\[
 \widehat\ell_{A,n}(x)=
 \max_{1\leq j\leq K}\sum_{a=1}^K
 \widehat M_A(x)_{aj}\mathbf 1\{\widehat M_A(x)_{aj}\leq\tau_{S,n}\},
 \qquad
 \ell_{A,n}=\|\widehat\ell_{A,n}\|_{L^2(P_X)},
\]
and define \(\widehat\ell_{Z,n}(x)\) and \(\ell_{Z,n}\) analogously from \(\widehat M_Z\).  These fitted low-mass functions are observable and their \(L^2(P_X)\) norms are estimable by foldwise empirical averaging.  If support sets \(S_A(x)\) and \(S_Z(x)\) are supplied as observed design information and the fit is constrained to vanish off those sets, define the corresponding leakage allowance to be zero.  No unknown true support is an input in either case.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The conditional-zero argument needs observable allowances for mass fitted into possible structural-zero cells.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient remains a pointwise \(K^2\)-cell projection followed by one conditional Gram solve. The implementable score now uses one non-oracle fitted product law: it never reads the true measurement supports or Gram rank, selects fitted Gram directions with the computable cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), and reports low-mass leakage allowances \(\ell_{A,n},\ell_{Z,n}\). The spectral solve is linearly stable, while structural-zero leakage enters the mean remainder additively and must be \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) unless support sets are genuinely supplied by the study design. Efficient cross-fitted Gaussian and maximum-\(t\) inference therefore uses explicit operator, support-screening, and leakage rates.

project_justification.fill: The project proves the conditional tangent-space and finite-projector results, then makes the attaining estimator non-oracle. A fixed \(\varepsilon/2\) spectral cutoff selects the fitted Gram rank on the separated event and has a linear integrated perturbation bound. An estimable low-mass diagnostic replaces hidden measurement-support knowledge: the conditional-zero algebra isolates additive surrogate and proxy leakage, and the remainder and inference conditions carry those terms explicitly. Known support sets are treated only as an optional observed-design specialization.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each training fold fits one label-aligned product law without using unknown measurement supports, the true conditional Gram matrix, or its rank. All posterior and projection objects are plug-in implications; the Gram inverse uses the fitted spectrum above \(\varepsilon/2\), and fitted low-mass measurement cells yield estimable support-leakage diagnostics.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator: their Theorems 2--4 treat the binary observed tangent space and influence functions, and Supplement S8.2 obtains the continuous-outcome efficiency bound through a refining outcome partition. The present multilevel construction instead uses the exact \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) and one conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) supply the categorical inverse-feature product-bridge precursor, but not observed-data canonicality or the non-oracle projected-score remainder. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009), Hu and Schennach (2008), and Deaner (2023) inform latent-factor identification; none supplies the conditional differential inverse or the support-leakage calculation used here. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform nuisance-score projection, Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement estimation, and Tsybakov (2009) informs the smooth sieve benchmark. The implementation result here does not assume access to a true measurement support or a true Gram rank; design-known supports are an optional specialization.
prose_updates.interpretation: The correction is finite-dimensional after conditioning on \(X\), but non-oracle implementation has two distinct regularity demands. Spectral separation makes rank selection benign: fitted eigenvalues above \(\varepsilon/2\) recover the true nonzero eigenspace when the Gram error is small. Structural zeros are different because a fitted probability placed in a latent class--measurement cell that is absent under the truth is not covered by the two-sided conditional-zero score restriction. Its fitted mass therefore appears as an additive, estimable leakage allowance rather than a quadratic product. In a validation design that records the support sets in advance, this allowance is exactly zero; otherwise it must be diagnosed and controlled at the inference rate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The non-oracle Gram correction is certified on the event \(\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\varepsilon/4\): thresholding at \(\varepsilon/2\) selects exactly the true number of nonzero directions, and the thresholded inverse differs from \(G^+\) by at most \(14\varepsilon^{-2}\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\); an unconditional conditional-\(L^2\) bound holds with constant \(26\varepsilon^{-2}\). For unknown measurement supports, \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) makes the low-mass screen cover all true structural-zero cells with high probability, but the resulting \(\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\) contribution is first order. Thus a generic coordinatewise smooth rate for the primitive factors does not by itself prove root-\(n\) inference when structural zeros are present.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact identification, tangent-space, finite-projector, canonical-gradient, strict-variance, binary-comparison, and continuous-witness claims remain restricted to the declared fixed-\(K\), separated, pathwise-interior model. The cross-fitted implementation uses no unknown measurement support and no oracle Gram rank. Its fitted Gram inverse is selected spectrally at \(\varepsilon/2\); score stability additionally tracks uniform Gram error. With unknown supports, inference requires both \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) and the corrected \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), whose additive leakage terms need not be quadratic. If the study protocol supplies support sets, enforcing those observed zeros sets the corresponding leakage allowances to zero. The smooth B-spline question must therefore establish primitive and derived operator rates, uniform support-screening rates, and sufficiently fast leakage; the old coordinatewise \(\rho_n\) assertion alone is not enough. Modal ties, local singularity, and support patterns that cannot be screened at the required rate remain outside efficient-inference delivery. The maternal-smoking application remains prospective because the published six-bin study does not itself verify paired-proxy conditional independence or design-known measurement supports.
